NOTES
Estimated Annual Bills (EAB) based on an annual usage of 4200 units
Day/Night Estimated Annual Bills are based on the advice of The Commission for the Regulation of Utilities (CRU) using the calculation with an assumption of 50% of electricity is consumed during the day and 50% is consumed at night.
Estimated Annual Bill
The Estimated Annual Bill is an easy-to-understand indicator for consumers. It is an estimate of the average household’s cost for electricity for a year and all energy-related charges such as the Standing Charge and PSO Levy for electricity.
The Estimated Annual Bill is based on the expected average consumption for one year. These figures are approved and published by the Commission for the Regulation of Utilities (CRU);
Electricity 4,200kWh
For electricity, the Estimated Annual Bill amount also takes into account the following information;
– Is your meter Urban or Rural?
– Is your meter 24 Hour or Day/Night?
An example of how the Estimated Annual Bill is calculated for an electricity Urban 24 Hour meter customer on our standard tariff, is given below. Note that the example is for illustrative purposes only and may not reflect current prices.
Unit rate of 53.00c x CRU's annual Consumption of 4200 units =
€2,226.00
Plus Annual Standing Charge =
€242.90
Annual PSO Levy =
€-89.10
Total Ex VAT
€2,379.80
Add VAT at 9%
€214.18
Estimated Annual Bill (EAB)
€2.593.98
Are you Urban or Rural?
Your bill can tell you this as ESB Networks classifies Urban customers as DG1 and Rural customers as DG2.
Do you have a 24 Hour or Day/night Meter?
Again your bill will help you identify the type of meter you have on your premises. The meter codes are represented with a Meter Configuration Code (MCC). The codes are:
MCC01: 24 Hour meter
MCC02: Day/Night meter
MCC03: 24 Hour meter with Night Storage Heating
MCC51: Day/Night meter with Night Storage Heating
Night Storage Heating?
This meter type is installed for clients who heat their homes with electricity.
As per the Commission for the Regulation of Utilities (CRU) customers with Night Storage Heating meters are assumed to use 50% of electricity by night.
SST
Energy kWh unit rates will be charged under the following time periods:
Day rate – electricity used between 08:00 – 17:00 everyday
Peak rate – electricity used between 17:00 – 19:00 everyday
Day rate – electricity used between 19:00 – 23:00 everyday
Night rate – electricity used between 23:00 – 08:00 everyday

<p><strong>NOTES</strong><br>Estimated Annual Bills (EAB) based on an annual usage of 4200 units</p>
<p>Day/Night Estimated Annual Bills are based on the advice of The Commission for the Regulation of Utilities (CRU) using the calculation with an assumption of 50% of electricity is consumed during the day and 50% is consumed at night.</p>
<p><em><strong>Estimated Annual Bill</strong></em></p>
<p>The Estimated Annual Bill is an easy-to-understand indicator for consumers. It is an estimate of the average household’s cost for electricity for a year and all energy-related charges such as the Standing Charge and PSO Levy for electricity.</p>
<p>The Estimated Annual Bill is based on the expected average consumption for one year. These figures are approved and published by the Commission for the Regulation of Utilities (CRU);</p>
<p>Electricity 4,200kWh</p>
<p>For electricity, the Estimated Annual Bill amount also takes into account the following information;<br>– Is your meter Urban or Rural?<br>– Is your meter 24 Hour or Day/Night?</p>
<p>An example of how the Estimated Annual Bill is calculated for an electricity Urban 24 Hour meter customer on our standard tariff, is given below. Note that the example is for illustrative purposes only and may not reflect current prices.</p>
<p>

<p><em><strong>Are you Urban or Rural?</strong></em></p>
<p>Your bill can tell you this as ESB Networks classifies Urban customers as DG1 and Rural customers as DG2.</p>
<p><em><strong>Do you have a 24 Hour or Day/night Meter?</strong></em></p>
<p>Again your bill will help you identify the type of meter you have on your premises. The meter codes are represented with a Meter Configuration Code (MCC). The codes are:<br><strong>MCC01: 24 Hour meter</strong><br><strong>MCC02: Day/Night meter</strong><br><strong>MCC03: 24 Hour meter with Night Storage Heating</strong><br><strong>MCC51: Day/Night meter with Night Storage Heating</strong></p>
<p><em><strong>Night Storage Heating?</strong></em><br>This meter type is installed for clients who heat their homes with electricity. </p>
<p>As per the Commission for the Regulation of Utilities (CRU) customers with Night Storage Heating meters are assumed to use 50% of electricity by night.</p>
<p><em><strong>SST</strong></em><br>Energy kWh unit rates will be charged under the following time periods:<br><strong>Day rate – electricity used between 08:00 – 17:00 everyday</strong><br><strong>Peak rate – electricity used between 17:00 – 19:00 everyday</strong><br><strong>Day rate – electricity used between 19:00 – 23:00 everyday</strong><br><strong>Night rate – electricity used between 23:00 – 08:00 everyday</strong></p>

Electrical Safety
Electricity can kill or severely injure people and cause damage to property. However, you can take simple precautions
when working with
or near electricity and electrical equipment to significantly reduce the risk of injury to you and others around you. A list of electrical safety information from ESB Networks is listed below:

	<header class="entry-header">
		<h1 class="entry-title">Electrical Safety</h1>	</header><!-- .entry-header -->

	<div class="entry-content">
		<p><span style="margin: 0px; color: #111111; font-family: 'Calibri Light',sans-serif; font-size: 10pt;">Electricity can kill or severely injure people and cause damage to property. However, you can take simple precautions </span><span style="margin: 0px; color: #111111; font-family: 'Calibri Light',sans-serif; font-size: 10pt;">when working with </span><span style="margin: 0px; color: #111111; font-family: 'Calibri Light',sans-serif; font-size: 10pt;">or near electricity and electrical equipment to significantly reduce the risk of injury to you and others around you. A list of electrical safety information from ESB Networks is listed below: </span></p>
<p><span style="color: #00ccff;"><span style="margin: 0px; font-family: 'Calibri Light',sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;"> </span><strong><span style="margin: 0px; font-family: 'Calibri Light',sans-serif;">ESB Networks General Safety Guidelines</span></strong></span><b></b></p>
<ul type="disc">

<li style="margin: 0px 0px 10.66px; color: #333333; line-height: normal; font-family: 'Calibri Light',sans-serif; font-size: 12pt; font-style: normal; font-weight: 400;"><span style="margin: 0px; font-family: 'Calibri Light',sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;"><a href="http://www.esb.ie/esbnetworks/en/safety-environment/safety_farm.jsp" target="esb" rel="noopener noreferrer">Safety on the Farm</a></span></li>

</div>
<p><span style="color: #00ccff;"><b><span style="margin: 0px; font-family: 'Calibri Light',sans-serif; font-size: 12pt;">ESB Networks website also has Safety Booklets freely available:</span></b></span></p>

Smart Meters
Smart Meter Data
What are the Smart Meters?
Smart meters are the next generation of electricity
meters. Using digital technology and the 2G mobile
phone network, the smart meter will give you access
to accurate information on your energy usage
throughout the day and significantly reduce the
need for estimated bills.
ESB Networks is replacing 2.4 million
electricity meters in homes, farms, and businesses across Ireland with next-generation meters.
This new technology which is already in use in over 500 million premises worldwide will bring
benefits to customers, the environment, and the economy.
When will the replacement programme be completed?
The programme is being delivered on a phased regional basis and was planned to be completed
in 2024. ESB began installations in autumn 2019 and by January 2021 approximately 245,000
smart meters were installed. As of January 2021, the deployment of the smart meter was
temporarily stopped due to Covid 19 restrictions so the rollout is expected to take longer than
originally stated.
FOR OUR CLIENTS:
If you are fortunate enough to have received an installation and would like access to your data,
please click on the below link, complete the questionnaire and we will get the data to you.
Request My HDF
Half Hour Data File (HDF)
Who can receive a Half Hourly Data File?
– You must be supplied electricity by Waterpower.
– You must be on our Waterpower Standard Smart Tariff (SST).
– You must be the registered account holder.
How do I receive my Half Hourly Data file?
– Click on the above button “Request my HDF ” and complete the form.
– If you have any questions, please contact us on the details below or see our FAQ.
– You must be the registered account holder.
What will be contained in my half-hourly consumption file?
– Up to 2 years’ worth of half hourly consumption data, only available from joining our Waterpower on the SST.
– The data is refreshed regularly by ESB, providing accurate up-to-date data from when you started with the SST.
– If you have switched from Waterpower’s SST day, night, and peak billing, the data will only be available once on the SST.

		<h1 class="entry-title">Smart Meters</h1>	</header><!-- .entry-header -->

	<div class="entry-content">
		<p><a href="https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/smart-meter.jpg"><picture fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" class="size-medium wp-image-1113 alignright">
<source type="image/webp" srcset="https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/smart-meter-300x168.jpg.webp 300w, https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/smart-meter-768x431.jpg.webp 768w, https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/smart-meter-500x280.jpg.webp 500w, https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/smart-meter-360x200.jpg.webp 360w, https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/smart-meter.jpg.webp 800w" sizes="(max-width: 300px) 100vw, 300px">
<img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" src="https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/smart-meter-300x168.jpg" alt="smart meter" width="300" height="168" srcset="https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/smart-meter-300x168.jpg 300w, https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/smart-meter-768x431.jpg 768w, https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/smart-meter-500x280.jpg 500w, https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/smart-meter-360x200.jpg 360w, https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/smart-meter-600x337.jpg 600w, https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2021/02/smart-meter.jpg 800w" sizes="(max-width: 300px) 100vw, 300px">
</picture>
</a><br>
Smart Meter Data</p>
<p>What are the Smart Meters?</p>
<p>Smart meters are the next generation of electricity<br>
meters. Using digital technology and the 2G mobile<br>
phone network, the smart meter will give you access<br>
to accurate information on your energy usage<br>
throughout the day and significantly reduce the<br>
need for estimated bills.</p>
<p>ESB Networks is replacing 2.4 million<br>
electricity meters in homes, farms, and businesses across Ireland with next-generation meters.<br>
This new technology which is already in use in over 500 million premises worldwide will bring<br>
benefits to customers, the environment, and the economy.</p>
<p>When will the replacement programme be completed?</p>
<p>The programme is being delivered on a phased regional basis and was planned to be completed<br>
in 2024. ESB began installations in autumn 2019 and by January 2021 approximately 245,000<br>
smart meters were installed. As of January 2021, the deployment of the smart meter was<br>
temporarily stopped due to Covid 19 restrictions so the rollout is expected to take longer than<br>
originally stated.</p>
<p>FOR OUR CLIENTS:</p>
<p>If you are fortunate enough to have received an installation and would like access to your data,<br>
please click on the below link, complete the questionnaire and we will get the data to you.</p>
<form action="https://www.waterpower.ie/request-my-hdf/"><button type="submit">Request My HDF</button></form>
<p> </p>
<p>Half Hour Data File (HDF)</p>
<p>Who can receive a Half Hourly Data File?</p>
<p>– You must be supplied electricity by Waterpower.</p>
<p>– You must be on our Waterpower Standard Smart Tariff (SST).</p>
<p>– You must be the registered account holder.</p>
<p>How do I receive my Half Hourly Data file?</p>
<p>– Click on the above button “Request my HDF ” and complete the form.</p>
<p>– If you have any questions, please contact us on the details below or see our FAQ.</p>
<p>– You must be the registered account holder.</p>
<p>What will be contained in my half-hourly consumption file?</p>
<p>– Up to 2 years’ worth of half hourly consumption data, only available from joining our Waterpower on the SST.</p>
<p>– The data is refreshed regularly by ESB, providing accurate up-to-date data from when you started with the SST.</p>
<p>– If you have switched from Waterpower’s SST day, night, and peak billing, the data will only be available once on the SST.</p>
<p>ESB Networks How to read your smart meter</p>

Home
About Us

Contact
Hydro-Electricity
Harnessing the power of water
Micro hydro
is a type of
hydroelectric power
that typically produces from 5 kW to 100 kW of electricity using the natural flow of water. Waterpower has been involved in the construction and retrofit of micro-hydro stations since 1985 and has a broad range of experience in the area. Our current electricity generation projects range from the restoration of a 10kW water wheel in Kildare to the design and construction of a 400kW hydroelectricity plant in Kerry. Our area of expertise extends beyond hydro and now includes electricity supply, working with auto-producers to purchase excess electricity (solar/wind/hydro) and rainwater harvesting projects.
What we can do for you?
• Support the design and construction of your build through guidance and project management.
• As an electricity supply company, we can support grid connection arrangements.
• We can purchase any excess electricity your system will produce at the standard market rates.
If you are interested in exploring the possibility of building a hydrostation on your land or have a historic site that you would like to bring back to life call Dan on 087 2616178

		<h1 class="entry-title">Hydro-Electricity</h1>	</header><!-- .entry-header -->

	<div class="entry-content">
		<figure id="attachment_275" aria-describedby="caption-attachment-275" style="width: 200px" class="wp-caption alignleft"><a href="https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/WATER.FLOW_.png"><img decoding="async" class="wp-image-275" src="https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/WATER.FLOW_-150x150.png" alt="WATER.FLOW" width="200" height="123" srcset="https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/WATER.FLOW_-600x369.png 600w, https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/WATER.FLOW_-300x184.png 300w, https://www.waterpower.ie/wp-content/uploads/2018/03/WATER.FLOW_.png 615w" sizes="(max-width: 200px) 100vw, 200px"></a><figcaption id="caption-attachment-275" class="wp-caption-text">Harnessing the power of water</figcaption></figure>
<p style="text-align: left;"><b>Micro hydro</b> is a type of <b>hydroelectric power</b> that typically produces from 5 kW to 100 kW of electricity using the natural flow of water. Waterpower has been involved in the construction and retrofit of micro-hydro stations since 1985 and has a broad range of experience in the area. Our current electricity generation projects range from the restoration of a 10kW water wheel in Kildare to the design and construction of a 400kW hydroelectricity plant in Kerry. Our area of expertise extends beyond hydro and now includes electricity supply, working with auto-producers to purchase excess electricity (solar/wind/hydro) and rainwater harvesting projects.</p>
<p><span style="color: #00ccff;">What we can do for you?</span></p>
<p style="text-align: left;">• Support the design and construction of your build through guidance and project management.<br>
• As an electricity supply company, we can support grid connection arrangements.<br>
• We can purchase any excess electricity your system will produce at the standard market rates.</p>
<p style="text-align: left;">If you are interested in exploring the possibility of building a hydrostation on your land or have a historic site that you would like to bring back to life call Dan on 087 2616178</p>

Electricity Generation
At Waterpower, we take care of your electricity needs from source to supply, giving you reliable, low-cost access to green energy. We have been designing and building hydro-electricity plants across Ireland since 2003, as well as generating and purchasing energy from wind and biomass sources, so you can depend on us for efficient, green electricity.
We buy from ten renewable energy producers across the country to meet our customer demand. It is our aim to source as much renewable energy as possible for our customers.
Do you generate your own electricity?
Do you produce more than you need?
Waterpower buys excess power from renewable energy generators thus If you are involved in
solar, wind, hydro
or
biomass
energy generating projects we would be delighted to speak with you.
Call us today
or email ellen.osullivan@waterpower.ie to find out more about our work with small renewable energy projects nationwide.
